feed.title: RFC: Two years of BIP Editing, time for some new faces?

entry.title: RFC: Two years of BIP Editing, time for some new faces?
entry.summary:
The backlog of BIP (Bitcoin Improvement Proposal) submissions has become increasingly challenging to manage, with several high-quality proposals remaining unread for extended periods. While contributions from non-editor reviewers like Daniela and Edil have alleviated some of the review workload, the team continues to fall behind, especially during times when editors are unavailable due to travel or personal commitments. The sustainability of the current arrangement is in question, as even increased individual efforts by existing editors have proven insufficient to keep pace with incoming submissions.
Two primary solutions are considered to address these challenges. The first is to expand the number of active BIP Editors, thereby distributing the workload more evenly and ensuring timely reviews and feedback for new proposals. The second option involves lowering editorial standards by restricting BIP Editors' responsibilities to format checks rather than thorough content reviews. However, maintaining rigorous review processes appears preferable to ensure the quality and integrity of accepted proposals.
A preferred approach emphasizes refreshing the team composition to include three actively engaged BIP Editors who regularly contribute to daily operations. To accommodate potential volunteers who may be hesitant about a long-term commitment, a term-limited arrangement—for example, serving as an editor for 12 to 24 months—could be offered. This structure aims to foster continuous participation while providing flexibility for contributors, ultimately supporting the efficiency and effectiveness of the BIP review process.
